trial_court: Family Court-cum-Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad, O.P.No.907 of 2017
case_name: Sangyam Vidya Sagar vs Sangyam Vandana
facts_of_case: The parties got married on 12.02.2017. The husband filed a petition under Section 12 (2) (b) (i) of Hindu Marriage Act to annul the marriage on grounds of cheating with dishonest intention and fraud played by the wife.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage can be annulled if the consent of the petitioner was obtained by fraud.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, by virtue of amendment dated 01.10.1978, or 'fraud' as to the nature of the ceremony or as to any material fact or circumstance concerning the respondent was included in Section 12 (1) (c) of the Act.

legal_principles.principle: A party's willingness to lead a marital life with the other party is relevant in determining the validity of the marriage.
legal_principles.held: I want to lead marital life with the appellant, for the sake of society to maintain respect in the society.

outcome.final_order: The trial court's order and decree dated 13.03.2020 were set aside, and the appeal was allowed.

keywords: Latin maxim: Falsus in uno, falsus in omnibus
use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for annulment of marriage due to fraud
advising client on grounds for divorce by fraud
researching case law on suppressed earlier marriages
